This resolution follows recent patterns: the Archdiocese of Los Angeles settled for more than $1 billion in 2024, and San Francisco agreed to $395 million in June. The Archdiocese secured funds through an uncommon insurance arrangement.

Terms allow each plaintiff to choose a lump-sum payment of at least $250,000 or seek a larger award after review of their claimed abuse. The Archdiocese must publish 'the names of the clergy members and lay leaders who were credibly accused of sexual abuse.'

Although all 1,300 plaintiffs have agreed to the proposal, spokesman Joseph Zwilling stated, 'We are not quite there yet.' Lawyers warned that rejecting the framework could trigger bankruptcy, reducing future payouts.
Spanning Manhattan, the Bronx, Staten Island, and parts of the Hudson Valley, The Archdiocese's settlement marks the latest in a series of major church resolutions addressing decades of abuse claims.

While the White House cautioned that formal policy changes remain subject to final administrative authorization, President Trump signaled during a Washington press conference that the U.S. is "very close" to a broader trade arrangement with Ottawa.

summary: On Sunday, President Donald Trump predicted during a Port Huron, Michigan, rally that the trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "pretty soon," claiming the nation is "willing to give us anything at this moment."

Diplomacy between Canada and the U.S. stalled in August when Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's government ended formal trade talks, prompting Washington to impose tariffs on billions in Canadian goods and Ottawa to levy retaliatory measures.

At the request of Republican Senator Susan Collins of Maine, Trump announced Friday he will lift some 50% tariffs at month's end while adding levies to dozens of new products, including Canadian garbage and sewage.

Republican Congressman Mike Rogers, running against Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed, has distanced himself from the president's tariff policy, saying "the automobile portion of these Canadian tariffs worries me a little bit."

With midterms less than two weeks away, the trade standoff remains a pivotal issue in Michigan's border region, where Trump won more than 66% of the vote in 2024 despite mounting economic pressure on the auto industry.

summary: On Sunday, Britain confirmed it will not join the Canada -led Defence Security and Resilience Bank , opting instead to pursue its own Multilateral Defence Mechanism for defence financing.

Ottawa spent months attempting to secure British participation, but the two governments could not agree on headquarters location, procurement levels, lending rules, and criteria for admitting new members.

Britain's Multilateral Defence Mechanism focuses on accelerating defence investment and joint procurement across NATO, while the DSRB emphasizes sovereign lending to support defence industries and supply chains.

Both countries agreed Sunday to develop a framework for cooperation, "having mutually concluded that it is best to develop two distinct but complementary institutions" to support each other on investment opportunities.
London will work in lockstep with Canada to meet NATO spending targets, while the Canada-based DSRB continues securing support from Belgium, Turkey, and Ukraine despite Britain's separate path.

title: Evacuations ordered within one mile of seafood plant fire on Newport’s Bayfront

summary: On Saturday night, Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries when another driver struck their vehicle, forcing her to postpone two stops on her "Alaska Always Tour."
Peltola is challenging Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan for the Alaska Senate seat in a highly competitive race where both candidates are competing for Alaska Native voters' support.
Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and President Donald Trump have labeled Peltola "No Show Mary," with Sullivan alleging she missed 20 percent of her votes while in office.
Campaign manager Cheryl Bruce stated Peltola is in "good spirits" following the accident but will reschedule Fairbanks and Bethel events; she remains "eager to get back on the campaign trail."

title: Alaska Democratic Senate Candidate Mary Peltola and Her Family Suffer Minor Injuries in Car Crash

summary: On Monday, the Israeli Air Force and the Shin Bet security agency announced they eliminated two Hamas commanders in the Gaza Strip during targeted airstrikes, accusing the group of systematically violating the ceasefire.

title: Israel Air Force Eliminates Two Hamas Commanders in Gaza Strikes Amid Ceasefire Violations

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Netanyahu’s “topple” and “overthrow” language as aggressive regime change, stressing escalation, covert action, and doubts that Israel can actually replace Iran’s government; its question-driven skepticism contrasts with right-leaning portrayals of removal as the “only way” to “guarantee future,” reinforced by Trump’s backing, nuclear fears, and warnings Iran could “burn.” Center coverage emphasizes the election context, repeating accusations of an “electoral circus” and “recklessly” politicized security.

summary: On Wednesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the only way to eliminate the nuclear threat "forever" is to overthrow the Iranian regime, instructing the army, Mossad, and security agencies to pursue this objective.

Netanyahu has described preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons as a primary campaign purpose, alongside creating conditions for Iranians to remove their rulers, previously declaring, "The regime must fall, and I will bring it down."

Simultaneously, Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a fresh threat, warning that "Iran will burn" if the Islamic Republic attacks Israel, claiming the regime is at its weakest point and may resort to extreme measures.

Referring to Mojtaba Khamenei, Netanyahu said: "Mojtaba Khamenei has chosen to follow in his father's footsteps," as Israel has long made clear it would welcome the fall of a regime committed to its destruction.

At the same ceremony, Chief of the General Staff Eyal Zamir emphasized the necessity of military unity, as the Israel Defense Forces continues efforts to recruit members of the ultra-Orthodox Jewish community.
title: Netanyahu says U.S. and Israel must topple Iranian regime

summary: On Wednesday, Premier Tony Wakeham endorsed Ithaca Energy's acquisition of Suncor's stakes in Newfoundland and Labrador's offshore oil projects, dismissing concerns about the company's ties as "political things."

Ithaca is majority-owned by the Delek Group, an Israeli conglomerate blacklisted by the United Nations for allegedly providing services supporting illegal settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

Assistant Professor of Law Heidi Matthews warns Ithaca's entry raises "serious liability questions" for the provincial government, as international law holds subnational jurisdictions accountable for assisting illegal occupations.
Michael Bueckert, vice president of Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East , calls the acquisition "unacceptable" and urges political leaders to impose sanctions.
Although Prime Minister Mark Carney committed to banning trade with illegal settlements in September, federal officials have yet to announce specific sanctions, leaving the policy's scope unclear.
title: N.L. Faces ‘Serious Liability Questions’ over Ithaca Energy’s Entry Into Province’s Oil Sector, Legal Expert Warns

title: Hassett Says US-Canada Trade Talks Are ‘Very Close’ to a Deal

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the nine-of-12 retention votes as a “major victory,” portraying boards as “quietly defying” Trump and Hegseth, transgender troops as facing “expulsion,” and resistance as potentially required against unlawful orders; it also foregrounds personal accounts and rhetoric such as “woke cadre” and “vilified.” Right-leaning coverage emphasizes “defy,” “ban,” and “troop ousters,” casting the votes as institutional resistance to executive authority and military policy.

summary: On Friday, The New York Times reported military review boards are defying orders from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to discharge transgender service members, with Navy and Marine Corps boards frequently voting to retain them.

President Donald Trump's administration created three-person separation boards with narrow instructions mandating dismissal of the estimated 4,250 transgender personnel currently serving in the military.

Navy and Marine Corps boards have voted to retain trans members in nine of 12 cases. Marine Staff Sgt. Damien Contreras saw board members cross out instructions regarding "a history of cross sex hormone therapy" and circle "remains qualified."

The Army and Air Force have overwhelmingly voted to discharge transgender service members, contrasting sharply with Navy and Marine retention rates. Board decisions are recommendations that politically appointed branch secretaries could reverse.

Rank-and-File soldiers are prioritizing service records over political mandates. "You have war fighters looking at war fighters," Contreras said, noting peers recognize colleagues who deployed and followed military rules.
title: Military boards are defying Hegseth’s orders to ban transgender troops: Report

title: Ukraine disputes Elon Musk’s claim that its military violated Starlink’s terms of service

summary: On Sunday, billionaire Bill Ackman called for Israel's next government to exclude National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, arguing their presence damages the nation's international standing.

Ackman warned that the ministers' controversial public statements are often interpreted abroad as reflecting the views of all Israelis, complicating efforts to rebuild trust and expand the Abraham Accords.
While praising Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's wartime leadership, Ackman emphasized he offered this perspective as someone who understands how Israel is perceived in the United States .
Responding to criticism, Ben-Gvir said diplomatic ties are important but should not supersede the nation's soldiers, while Ackman called for a moderate centrist coalition after the elections.

Following his visit to Sheba Medical Center with Director General Prof. Yitshak Kreiss, Ackman expressed confidence in Israel's technological potential and prospects for normalization with Saudi Arabia.
title: Bill Ackman says Ben-Gvir, Smotrich should not serve in next Israeli government

bias: Left-Leaning coverage portrays Trump’s attack on Lisa Murkowski as a volatile, retaliatory outburst, using terms like “manic,” “midnight meltdown,” and “stupid” to question his temperament and suggest contempt for voters, while recalling her impeachment vote.

Right-Leaning coverage instead frames the dispute around ranked-choice voting, similar-named candidates, the “incumbent” label, and a “plant candidate,” presenting Trump’s concerns as election-mechanics objections; “castigates” and “rips” reinforce confrontation.
Center coverage emphasizes the institutional lawsuit and escalating political fight, attributing “disgrace” and “worst senator” to Trump.

summary: President Donald Trump attacked Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski late Saturday, calling her a "disgrace" after she publicly criticized a federal lawsuit blocking Alaska's Senate election certification.

The DOJ lawsuit, which Trump personally directed, seeks to halt certification if incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan loses to Democratic candidate Mary Peltola. Officials contend that Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a similarly named candidate, could siphon critical votes from the Trump-backed incumbent.

Rejecting the administration's intervention, Murkowski stated the Justice Department "should never have filed this lawsuit" on Friday. Trump countered by calling Alaska's ranked-choice voting system a "TOTAL DEMOCRAT SCAM."

Polling shows Peltola leading Sullivan 51 percent to 49 percent in a simulated final round of ranked-choice voting. Trump warned Alaskans that a Democratic victory would halt his previous achievements for the state.

Alaska voters will decide the election system's future through Ballot Measure 2, which proposes repealing ranked-choice voting. Both state and Alaska Supreme Court rulings have previously dismissed efforts to remove Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. from the ballot.
title: Trump calls Murkowski a ‘disgrace’ to Alaska, criticizes ranked choice voting
